newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished higher on Friday as foreign investors rediscovered the guilder market after a long time away, dealers said.
"Quite a few international buyers are stepping in at these levels," one said, adding the five-year yield spread to Bunds was seen as attractive.
They said most activity had been concentrated at the end of the mid-curve, up to 2007 paper.
Early trade was helped by German June inflation data in line with expectations, with U.S. PPI numbers lifting prices later.
"We went up like a rocket after the PPI, but after that we fell back somewhat on profit-taking," a dealer said.
Investors came back to guilders after the Bund future shed some gains, he added.
Dealers said Thursday's surprise 10 basis point hike in the Dutch special advances rate to 3.0 percent in line with its German equivalent had had no impact.
"The timing was a little surprising, but the move itself was not," a dealer said. "That had long been expected by the market."
